report:
# FQ-POWER-RULE-P2-SELECTION

The old even-exponent theorem 2=2^k is not the declared real (3/5,4/5) power equation. A new Real.rpow theorem proves that equation iff p=2 on the admitted real-power domain. Native integer powers use psi=(1,1,0) and bases sharing e1, with the other two basis vectors rotated by the exact (3,4,5) triangle. The original claim about p=1 Sorkin vanishing needs a sign restriction: |t| gives I3(1,1,-1)=2, while I3(1,1,1)=0. No general Gleason theorem or primitive selection is supplied.

Supported: The real power equation (3/5)^p+(4/5)^p=1 iff p=2 is kernel checked. Integer p=1..8 reproduce actual shared-ray context weights; mixed-sign p=1 supplies a retained counterexample to unrestricted Sorkin vanishing.

Remaining: The power-law family, real exponentiation and the real orthonormal contexts are admitted; formal transport of the concrete context normalization to the Real.rpow equation remains a separate bridge. No unrestricted readout uniqueness or Gleason theorem follows.
